runs.market_commentary:
Asian equity markets closed mixed-to-lower on Friday after Thursday's broad Wall Street selloff. The Nikkei 225 slipped 0.31% to 66,008, weighed by elevated US Treasury yields and risk-off sentiment stemming from escalating US-Iran geopolitical tensions that have pushed WTI crude to approximately $93/barrel. Germany's DAX fell 0.42% to 25,983 — European industrials and autos face a double headwind from higher energy costs and a hawkish US Fed. The FTSE 100 managed a marginal +0.04% gain to 10,748, benefiting from oil-sector heavyweights (BP, Shell) as a partial offset to broader risk aversion.

US futures are recovering modestly Friday morning, with S&P 500 futures up ~0.32%, Nasdaq-100 futures +0.60%, and Dow futures +0.60% — partially retracing Thursday's sharp losses (SPX -0.84%, DJIA -1.27%). The macro backdrop remains challenging: the 10-year Treasury yield holds at 4.71% after Tuesday's FOMC minutes confirmed a hawkish tilt, with markets pricing only a 35% probability of a rate cut at the next meeting, down sharply from ~64% a month ago. Treasury Secretary Bessent's 'economic warfare' against Iran adds an inflationary overlay that complicates any Fed pivot narrative. WTI near $93 keeps the Fed firmly on hold regardless of softening in jobs or growth data.

On the micro side, today's session features sharp cross-currents in retail. Walmart cratered 9.15% to $103.84 on Thursday — one of its largest single-day drops in recent memory — signaling a significant earnings or guidance miss and raising red flags about the US consumer. Advance Auto Parts collapsed 24.55% to $42.39, suggesting severe fundamental deterioration. These two datapoints together paint a cautionary picture. The silver lining: crypto is surging, with Bitcoin +7.86% to $74,902 and XRP +18.90%, and off-price retailer Ross Stores is highlighted as a pre-market focus name — a classic beneficiary of the trade-down dynamic when full-price retail disappoints.

ideas.catalyst: Trump administration announced 'economic warfare' against Iran, with Treasury Secretary Bessent touting the toughest-ever sanctions regime, structurally elevating defense demand.
ideas.thesis: Lockheed Martin is the premier defense prime with direct exposure to Iran-related military posturing, from F-35 demand to missile defense systems. Escalating Middle East tensions historically drive LMT outperformance relative to the broader market, and the current geopolitical trajectory supports sustained defense spending increases through 2027.
ideas.key_risk: Diplomatic resolution or ceasefire removes the geopolitical premium and drives a sharp rotation out of defense names.

ideas.catalyst: Goldman Sachs added Aon to its August Conviction Buy List with a $430 price target implying ~21% upside, citing NFP acquisition synergies and above-consensus free cash flow for 2026-2027.
ideas.thesis: Aon's integration of NFP is generating ahead-of-schedule synergies in the mid-market insurance segment, with Goldman projecting FCF materially above consensus through 2027. The capital markets recovery provides an additional tailwind for Aon's financial advisory and risk management businesses.
ideas.key_risk: Macro slowdown reduces commercial insurance demand; NFP integration delays or cost overruns emerge.

ideas.catalyst: Goldman Sachs added Capital One to its August Conviction List projecting ~28% upside on strong Q2 results and improving credit quality metrics.
ideas.thesis: Capital One's Q2 results demonstrated improving delinquency trends and expanding net interest margins as the rate environment stabilizes at elevated levels. With Goldman projecting ~28% upside and the market still pricing a significant credit risk premium, COF offers attractive risk/reward for investors willing to look through near-term consumer uncertainty.
ideas.key_risk: A recession or unemployment spike causes credit deterioration faster than expected, driving delinquency rates sharply higher.

ideas.catalyst: AAP collapsed 24.55% to $42.39 on Thursday on heavy volume, signaling a severe earnings miss or material guidance cut that typically triggers further analyst target reductions.
ideas.thesis: A 24% single-session drop in Advance Auto Parts points to fundamental deterioration — margin compression, inventory issues, or demand deceleration — that rarely resolves within days. Analyst estimate resets and institutional selling typically extend the pain over subsequent sessions, making the stock a compelling near-term momentum short.
ideas.key_risk: Value buyers and short-squeeze dynamics drive a sharp relief bounce from deeply oversold levels.

ideas.catalyst: Walmart fell 9.15% to $103.84 Thursday, one of its largest single-day drops in recent memory, signaling a meaningful earnings miss or forward guidance cut below consensus.
ideas.thesis: A 9%+ drop in Walmart — historically a defensive bellwether — signals either a fundamental earnings miss or a forward guidance reset that will require sell-side estimate reductions and additional institutional selling. The defensive premium embedded in WMT's valuation may further decompress if the consumer spending narrative deteriorates across the sector.
ideas.key_risk: The stock has already discounted the bad news; any positive management tone or analyst defense drives a sharp reversal from oversold levels.

ideas.catalyst: Ross Stores flagged as a pre-market focus name Friday as Walmart's 9.15% collapse signals consumer fatigue at full-price retail, driving the trade-down dynamic that historically benefits off-price formats.
ideas.thesis: Ross Stores is a structural beneficiary whenever full-price retail disappoints, as budget-constrained consumers reallocate spending to value channels. With Walmart's miss and broader consumer spending under pressure from Iran-driven inflation and elevated interest rates, Ross's comp store sales trajectory should outperform peers in H2 2026.
ideas.key_risk: A broad consumer recession hits all retail formats equally; inventory availability shrinks as brand partners reduce close-outs.

ideas.catalyst: Bitcoin surged 7.86% to $74,902 and XRP rallied 18.90% Friday, signaling renewed broad-based risk appetite in digital assets heading into the weekend.
ideas.thesis: Coinbase is the highest-beta liquid US equity proxy for crypto market upswings. Bitcoin approaching $75K is a key psychological level; a sustained break higher would drive significant retail and institutional FOMO, boosting Coinbase's trading volumes and transaction fee revenue materially above current consensus estimates.
ideas.key_risk: Weekend crypto volatility reverses sharply on regulatory news or broader risk-off; BTC fails to hold $70K support.

ideas.catalyst: Iran geopolitical escalation and the Trump 'economic warfare' plan are driving safe-haven demand for gold, with oil at $93 reinforcing the inflationary case for precious metals.
ideas.thesis: Newmont offers leveraged exposure to gold's safe-haven bid at a time when the Iran-US standoff shows no signs of near-term resolution. With the Fed unable to cut rates amid inflationary oil prices, gold miners benefit from both rising gold prices and a ceiling on the real rate headwind that typically weighs on the sector.
ideas.key_risk: Sudden diplomatic resolution to the Iran crisis deflates the geopolitical risk premium; the US dollar strengthens sharply.

ideas.catalyst: ASML flagged as a notable Friday mover; as the world's only supplier of EUV lithography systems, any positive semiconductor demand signal carries outsized order-book implications.
ideas.thesis: ASML is a structural long as the irreplaceable supplier of extreme ultraviolet lithography equipment required for advanced chip manufacturing at 3nm and below. AI-driven semiconductor capex continues to drive multi-year backlog accumulation; any Friday mover catalyst likely reflects a positive datapoint in the chip demand cycle that reinforces the long thesis.
ideas.key_risk: Semiconductor demand cycle turns down, delaying orders; additional US export control restrictions to China reduce ASML's addressable market.

ideas.catalyst: FOMC minutes released August 19 confirmed hawkish tilt with only 35% cut probability; 10-year Treasury holds at 4.71% with Iran oil shock adding inflationary pressure.
ideas.thesis: Long-duration Treasuries face a persistently unfavorable environment with the 10-year anchored at 4.71%, the Fed firmly on hold, and an oil shock from the Iran situation adding upside risk to inflation. TLT's price is inversely correlated to yields, and with limited near-term catalyst for a rate cut, the path of least resistance for yields remains elevated or higher.
ideas.key_risk: A risk-off panic or recession scare drives a flight-to-safety rally in Treasuries, sharply compressing yields and causing losses on the short position.

deals.headline: Trump Administration Announces 'Economic Warfare' Sanctions Against Iran
deals.description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced the administration's 'toughest-ever' sanctions regime against Iran, framed as economic warfare. The move is driving WTI crude to approximately $93/barrel and creating significant cross-asset ripples across energy, defense, and safe-haven assets globally.
deals.impact: Bullish for energy, defense, and gold; bearish for rate-sensitive sectors and consumer stocks

deals.headline: Goldman Sachs Adds AON, COF, BAC to August Conviction Buy List
deals.description: Goldman Sachs added three financial sector names to its August 2026 Conviction Buy List: Aon plc (PT $430, ~21% upside), Capital One Financial (~28% upside), and Bank of America. The additions are driven by above-consensus FCF at Aon, strong Q2 results at Capital One, and capital markets recovery tailwinds across the sector.
deals.impact: Near-term positive price catalyst for all three names; expected institutional buying

deals.headline: Madison Air Acquires Airflow Technologies for $5.4 Billion
deals.description: HVAC distribution company Madison Air announced the acquisition of Airflow Technologies in a $5.4 billion all-cash deal signed August 18. Both companies are privately held, limiting direct public market impact, but the deal size signals continued industrial distribution consolidation appetite and a healthy M&A premium environment.
deals.impact: Read-through positive for HVAC/industrial distribution peers; signals sector M&A premium

deals.headline: Alibaba Divests Video Game Division for $1.5B+
deals.description: Alibaba Group (BABA) announced the sale of its video game business for at least $1.5 billion as the company continues streamlining its portfolio to focus on core e-commerce and cloud operations. The divestiture reduces the conglomerate discount and improves capital allocation optionality for shareholders.
deals.impact: Mildly positive for BABA; asset monetization supports balance sheet and reduces complexity discount

deals.headline: Lyntris Defense Prices Downsized US IPO at $298 Million
deals.description: Defense contractor Lyntris completed a downsized US IPO raising approximately $298 million, below its initial target, suggesting measured institutional demand at the initial price range. Defense sector tailwinds from the Iran geopolitical escalation could support aftermarket trading and the broader defense IPO pipeline.
deals.impact: Positive read-through for defense sector peers; watch RTX and NOC for sympathy moves
